title: Nodal families admit regular affine curve presentations
statement:
Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $f:X\to S$ a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Assume its geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are nonempty reduced schemes pure of dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension] and are nodal: every closed point outside the smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of the geometric fibre has maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] isomorphic to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] over the algebraically closed geometric field $\Omega$. The geometric fibres need not be connected. Every ordinary residue-field fibre is pure of dimension one and a local complete intersection over its residue field [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ and every $x\in f^{-1}V$, there is an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset f^{-1}V$ of $x$ and an integer $c\geq0$ with an $R$-algebra presentation
$$B\simeq R[x_0,\ldots,x_c]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$$
whose ordered equations are a regular sequence in the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Thus these are regular affine curve presentations of [def-trf-nodal-dualizing-datum], covering $f^{-1}V$ for every such $V$. The coefficient map is the one induced by $f$. Neither properness, connectedness, a smooth generic fibre, a marking, nor a normal or integral base is required.

source.place: Tags 00SY (lemma-syntomic), 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal), 061L (lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood), together with curves.tex Tag 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci). Agent assembly of former item steps 1--3; use yh-1 to express a principal ambient localization as a regular affine curve presentation.

proof.text: Every ordinary or geometric field fibre is locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). On its affine opens [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives finitely presented algebras over the field, hence finitely generated algebras (discard the finitely many relations). By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] these fibres are locally of finite type.

Fix a geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$. It is locally of finite type by step 1 and pure of dimension one by hypothesis. Every closed point is smooth or has precisely the completed node ring in [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion](1); use $\Omega$ itself as its algebraic closure. The implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) gives a local complete intersection over $\Omega$. This holds for every geometric fibre and does not require connectedness.

By [lem-trf-geometric-pure-fibre-point-dimension], every ordinary fibre $X_s$ has local topological dimension $1$ at every point. Apply the component formula of [lem-trf-field-extension-component-local-dimension] to $Y=X_s$ and the identity extension $\kappa(s)/\kappa(s)$: every irreducible component has dimension $1$, so $X_s$ is pure of dimension one. The same argument applies to every nonempty open subscheme of $X_s$: its local topological dimensions agree with those of $X_s$, since neighbourhoods contained in an open neighbourhood are cofinal in the definition of local topological dimension. Thus every nonempty affine open in an ordinary fibre has dimension $1$ as well.

Fix $s\in S$, an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ containing $s$, with prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ corresponding to $s$, and an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq f^{-1}V$. Let $\Omega=\overline{\kappa(s)}$ be the algebraic closure fixed in [def-weil-geometric-fibre], so that the geometric fibre of the hypothesis is $X_{\bar s}=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$; note that only this geometric fibre is controlled by the hypotheses, not the fibres at arbitrary algebraically closed fields. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] $A\to B$ is of finite presentation, so $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a finitely generated $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra (the images of the variables generate it). By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] the inverse images of $U$ in $X_s$ and in $X_{\bar s}$ are open subschemes and are the fibre products $U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, $U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$; as $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ factor through the open $V$, these are $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, which [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\Omega)$ over the respective fields. By step 2, $X_{\bar s}$ has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated local-complete-intersection $\Omega$-algebras, so [lem-trf-lci-affine-open-locality], applied to the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\Omega)$, shows that $B\otimes_A\Omega$ is a local complete intersection over $\Omega$. Since $(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\Omega\cong B\otimes_A\Omega$ as $\Omega$-algebras ($(b\otimes t)\otimes u\mapsto b\otimes tu$, inverse $b\otimes u\mapsto(b\otimes1)\otimes u$), the converse direction of [lem-weil-pbc-lci-field-change] shows that $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] the affine opens $U\subseteq f^{-1}V$ cover $f^{-1}V\supseteq f^{-1}(s)$, so their inverse images, the affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ just described, cover $X_s$: this proves the ordinary-fibre LCI assertion. As $X_s$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(s)$ by step 1, (1)$\Rightarrow$(3) of [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion] shows that each $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $\kappa(s)$.

proof.text: Fix the prescribed $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $x\in f^{-1}V$, and set $s=f(x)$. The local ring map at $x$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism], and $f$ is of finite presentation at $x$. Together with step 4 these are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-trf-syntomic-pointwise-local-model]. Obtain an affine neighbourhood $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0\subset f^{-1}V$ of $x$ and $B_0=P/(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, a relative global complete intersection as an $R$-algebra via $f$. Its fibre over $s$, $\operatorname{Spec}(B_0\otimes_R\kappa(s))$, is a nonempty (it contains $x$) affine open in $X_s$ by the chart identification of step 4, so has dimension $1$ by step 3. The relative-global-CI condition [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection] gives $n-r=1$, hence $n=r+1$.

Let $q\subset B_0$ be the point $x$, and $q\prime\subset P$ its inverse image. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence], the ordered $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ form a regular sequence in $P_{q\prime}$. The ring $R$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], and $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Hence [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood] gives $h\in P\setminus q\prime$ such that the $a_i$ form a regular sequence in $P_h$. Put $g=h\bmod(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$. Since $g\notin q$, [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] identifies $U=\operatorname{Spec}(B_0)_g$ with an affine open neighbourhood of $x$ in $U_0$.

In $P[y]$, multiplication by $hy-1$ is injective: if $(hy-1)\sum b_i y^i=0$, coefficient comparison gives $b_0=0$ and $b_i=hb_{i-1}=0$ inductively. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient], $P[y]/(hy-1)\simeq P_h$. Thus $hy-1,a_1,\ldots,a_r$ is a regular sequence by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], since after its first element its successive multiplication maps are those of the regular sequence in $P_h$. Its final quotient is $(B_0)_g$: equivalently quotient first by the $a_i$ and apply the same localization presentation to $B_0$ and $g$. This quotient is nonzero because it has the point $x$. Set $c=r+1$. There are $n+1=r+2=c+1$ variables and $c$ ordered equations, as required. Every map fixes $R$, so the coefficient map is induced by $f$. Repeating for each $x$ gives the asserted cover.
